mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the previous 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL increases above 2.5% annualized and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% over the previous month signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases by more than 1% and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% over the previous month signals a weakening supply side, which may lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to concerns about economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases by more than 0.5% and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is below 1% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points combined with an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the previous 3 months signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decrease > 0.5pp and PAYEMS increase > 200k in 3 months
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp and PAYEMS increases by more than 200k and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where an increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the previous 3 months signals strong demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, but only during economic expansions.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases by more than 5% during an economic expansion and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a decrease in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% combined with a decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% over the previous 3 months signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decrease > 0.5% and GDPC1 decrease > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: If INDPRO and GDPC1 both decrease by more than 0.5% and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.
